name: io.github.cyanheads/smithsonian-mcp-server
description: Search 14.5M Smithsonian Open Access objects, get CC0 images, find cross-collection connections.

tools.name: smithsonian_search_objects
tools.description: Recommended first step for open-ended or topic discovery: free-text search across 14.5 million Smithsonian objects, with optional exact filters. Filters narrow by museum unit, object type, indexed date term, culture, geographic place, subject topic, named party, scientific name, media type, online/CC0 availability, and objects on display now. Returns curated summaries (title, date, museum, thumbnail URL, CC0 flag) with the total match count. The record_id in each result is the identifier for smithsonian_get_object, smithsonian_find_related, and smithsonian_get_media. To browse one exact category — a single museum, culture, date term, object type, or topic — use smithsonian_browse_category instead.

query.description: Free-text search. Every word is required — OR does not widen a search, while NOT excludes. Use specific terms for precision ("Tlingit totem pole") or broad terms for browsing ("quilt").

filters.description: Optional structured filters to narrow the search. A key outside this set is rejected by name.

unit_code.description: Museum unit code (e.g. "NASM", "SAAM", "NMAH", "NMAAHC", "NMAI", "NPG", "CHNDM", "SIL"); the National Museum of Natural History is indexed under discipline sub-units like "NMNHBIRDS" and "NMNHPALEO", not a bare "NMNH". The full set is enumerable via smithsonian_list_terms (field "unit_code").

object_type.description: Object type term from Smithsonian's controlled vocabulary — commonly plural (e.g. "Paintings", "Photographs", "Aircraft"). Singular everyday forms like "Painting" usually return nothing. This field is not enumerable via smithsonian_list_terms; harvest valid values from the object_type field in smithsonian_search_objects results or from smithsonian_get_object indexed.object_type. Matched exactly and case-sensitively, and casing variants are indexed as SEPARATE categories — "button" and "Button" each hold their own records, and neither casing is reliably the larger — so probe a harvested value's other casings rather than assuming one covers the concept.

date.description: Indexed date term. Decades ("1920s", "1960s") are the most common form, but the vocabulary also carries year ranges ("500-1500"), century terms ("21st century"), and BCE forms ("-2500", "BCE 1000s"). The value must be an exact term — the full set is enumerable via smithsonian_list_terms (field "date").

culture.description: Culture term from the controlled vocabulary — often plural or qualified (e.g. "Aztecs", "Plains Indian"). The vocabulary is enumerable via smithsonian_list_terms (field "culture").

place.description: Geographic place term, matched exactly (e.g. "United States"). Variants are separate terms with no hierarchy — "United States of America" is a different, far smaller term, and a record filed under a state alone carries no country term. The full set is enumerable via smithsonian_list_terms (field "place").

topic.description: Subject term from the controlled vocabulary (e.g. "Quilts", "Aviation"). Matches the indexed.topic values smithsonian_get_object returns; its topics[] also carries free-text subject strings ("Quilts--History") that match nothing here. A hard constraint — topic "Quilts" matches 1,134 objects where the same word as free text matches 2,677. The full set is enumerable via smithsonian_list_terms (field "topic").

name.description: Indexed named party — maker, collector, donor, issuing authority, or any other role the catalog records. Written surname-first (e.g. "Warhol, Andy"). This field is not enumerable via smithsonian_list_terms. Take the exact value from smithsonian_get_object indexed.name, which lists every party a record is indexed under; its makers[] is the free-text form of the same parties and is often written differently ("Neil A. Armstrong" for the indexed "Armstrong, Neil A."), and a differently written name matches nothing here.

online_only.description: When true, restrict to records carrying an indexed online_media_type value. That vocabulary covers digitized surrogates — finding aids, catalog cards, scanned books, full text, electronic resources — alongside images, 3D models, and video, and the surrogate types often have no deliverable media attached, so a match can still report has_media: false. Read has_media on each result to decide whether smithsonian_get_media will return anything.

scientific_name.description: Exact indexed scientific name from smithsonian_get_object.scientific_names, e.g. "Crotalus horridus"; a bare genus ("Crotalus") also matches, across its species. Not enumerable via smithsonian_list_terms.

online_media_type.description: Exact indexed media category from smithsonian_list_terms { field: "online_media_type" }, e.g. "Images", "3D Models", "Sound recordings". Even Images does not guarantee attached or CC0 images; read smithsonian_get_object.media_summary for availability.

cc0_only.description: When true, restrict to records that have CC0-licensed media attached (the Lucene term media_usage:CC0). This selects on media presence, not license status — the roughly 9.2M records it excludes are CC0 too, they simply have nothing digitized. Read has_media on each result to decide whether smithsonian_get_media will return anything.

on_view_only.description: When true, restrict to objects the catalog flags as on physical display now (onPhysicalExhibit "Yes", about 13,000 records from 13 museums); smithsonian_get_object current_exhibitions names where. Most records carry no flag at all, so an unflagged object may still be on view, and there is no off-view filter. false or omitted adds nothing.

rows.description: Page size (default 20). A value above 1000 is served at 1000 with a notice.

start.description: Pagination offset — 0-indexed. Use with rows for paging through large result sets.

tools.name: smithsonian_list_terms
tools.description: Enumerate the valid term vocabulary for an indexed Smithsonian filter field (unit_code, culture, place, date, online_media_type, topic). Terms are a controlled vocabulary — often plural or qualified (e.g. "Paintings", not "Painting") — so guessed filter values tend to return nothing. Returns a page of the field's distinct term values; large vocabularies (topic has 133k terms, place 114k) page via start and rows. For unit_code, each code is returned with its museum name and contains matches the name as well as the code, so a museum name resolves to its code in one call.

field.description: Indexed field to enumerate. Choices: unit_code (museum codes like "NASM"), culture (e.g. "Aztecs"), place (geographic terms), date (decade/era values like "1920s"), online_media_type (media formats like "Images", "3D Models"), topic (subject terms like "Quilts" — 133k terms, so pair it with contains).

start.description: Pagination offset (0-indexed). Use with rows to page through large vocabularies.

rows.description: Number of terms to return per page (default 50). A value above 40000 is served at 40000 with a notice.

contains.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on the term vocabulary — resolve a filter value (e.g. "greek") to its exact controlled-vocabulary term(s). For unit_code it also matches each code's museum name and the names a unit also goes by (National Museum of Natural History for the NMNH divisions, Freer Gallery of Art and Arthur M. Sackler Gallery for NMAA, Cooper-Hewitt, National Design Museum for CHNDM and CHSDM), ignoring a leading "Smithsonian", "&" versus "and", apostrophe style, and hyphens versus spaces, so "Smithsonian National Air & Space Museum" resolves to "NASM".

tools.name: smithsonian_get_object
tools.description: Fetch a normalized catalog metadata projection for a Smithsonian object by its record_id (from smithsonian_search_objects results). Returns title, dates, description, labeled notes, makers, the labeled physical description (materials, measurements, specimen attributes such as sex and preparation), places, cultures, topics, exhibition history, current display (on_view and current_exhibitions, for objects the catalog flags), the sets the catalog files it under (collections, departments, and for displayed objects the gallery or exhibition), credit line, identifiers, rights, and a media summary. indexed carries the exact name, place, object_type, date, and topic values the record is indexed under, each passable verbatim to the smithsonian_search_objects filter of the same name — the free-text makers, places, dates, and topics often differ from them. Natural-history records can include scientific_names, taxonomy, and collection coordinates without inferred precision. The media summary counts the media and links every non-image item (3D models, scanned books, documents); full image URLs come from smithsonian_get_media, and the model files of a 3d_voyager item from smithsonian_get_media with media: "3d".

tools.name: smithsonian_get_media
tools.description: Return a Smithsonian object's CC0 (open-access) images at multiple resolutions, in catalog order, with cc0_image_count — or, with media: "3d", its CC0 3D model packages with cc0_model_count. In the default images mode, an object with no CC0 image fails with its own reason: nothing digitized, media that is entirely non-image (3D models, scanned books, documents; a 3D object's failure names the media: "3d" call), or images that are all non-CC0. Page a long list with start and limit: omit limit to get everything from start, and a start at or past the count returns an empty list. Each image includes a thumbnail (~150px), a screen-size image (~1,200px on the long edge), and a full-size JPEG — with pixel dimensions when the catalog lists a high-resolution JPEG — plus an archival TIFF when one exists. Each 3D package carries its Voyager viewer URL, a thumbnail, and its downloadable files: URL, filename, resolution tier (low, full, iOS AR, or watertight for 3D printing), file and mesh format, units, Draco compression, and size in bytes, spelled as the catalog lists them. A record with no 3D package fails no_models in 3D mode. On smithsonian_search_objects, the cc0_only filter surfaces objects with downloadable CC0 images, and filters.online_media_type "3D Models" surfaces objects with 3D packages.

id.description: record_id of the object (e.g. "nasm_A19670093000") from smithsonian_search_objects or smithsonian_get_object.

media.description: Which media to return: "images" for CC0 images, or "3d" for CC0 3D model packages and their downloadable model files.

start.description: Offset into the CC0 images, or with media "3d" the CC0 model packages, 0-indexed in catalog order. A truncated page names the next start in its notice.

limit.description: Images, or with media "3d" model packages, to return from start. Omit to return every one from start. A value above 1000 is served at 1000 with a notice.

tools.name: smithsonian_browse_category
tools.description: Browse Smithsonian objects within one exact category — a single museum (mode "museum"), culture, indexed date term (mode "period"), object type (mode "medium"), or subject term (mode "topic"). The value must be an exact indexed category term, not free text: resolve museum, culture, period, and topic vocabulary with smithsonian_list_terms first (object_type is not enumerable there — take the exact terms of a known object from smithsonian_get_object indexed.object_type, or harvest them from smithsonian_search_objects results, and treat each casing as its own category, since an object_type term covers only the casing it was written in). Returns the category total count, a page of matching objects, and a museum breakdown of that page; page the full category with start and rows. For open-ended or topic discovery, start with smithsonian_search_objects instead.

mode.description: Browse dimension: "museum" (by unit code), "culture" (by culture term), "period" (by indexed date term like "1940s" or "500-1500"), "medium" (by object type like "Paintings"), "topic" (by subject term like "Quilts").

value.description: Category value appropriate to the mode. museum: a unit code like "NASM", "SAAM", or "NMNHBIRDS", matched literally and case-sensitively — not a museum name. culture: term, often plural or qualified ("Aztecs", "Plains Indian"). period: an indexed date term — commonly a decade ("1940s", "1860s"), but year ranges ("500-1500"), century terms ("21st century"), and BCE forms ("-2500", "BCE 1000s") are indexed too. medium: object type, usually plural ("Paintings", "Aircraft"). topic: subject term ("Quilts", "Aviation"). Smithsonian uses a controlled vocabulary — for museum (unit_code), culture, period (date), and topic, call smithsonian_list_terms to find exact terms; medium (object_type) is not enumerable there, so take the exact terms of a known object from smithsonian_get_object indexed.object_type, or harvest them from smithsonian_search_objects results. Every mode matches its value exactly and case-sensitively, and for medium that split is load-bearing: casing variants are indexed as SEPARATE categories, each reporting its own total_count ("button" and "Button" are different categories, and neither casing is reliably the larger), so browse the variants of an object_type term rather than assuming one covers the concept.

rows.description: Number of sample objects to return (default 10). A value above 1000 is served at 1000 with a notice.

start.description: Pagination offset — 0-indexed. Page contiguously by advancing start by the number of objects returned; a truncated page names the next start in its notice.

tools.name: smithsonian_find_related
tools.description: Discover objects across Smithsonian collections related to a given anchor object, matched on shared metadata signals — culture, period, object type, named parties, and topic terms. Each related object is tagged with the signals that connected it to the anchor; a named-party signal carries the catalog's own role for that party (maker, Collector, Donor, issuing authority, …), not a fixed "maker" label. Matches surface across museums — an NASM aerospace anchor can pull related objects from NMNHPALEO, SAAM, and NMAH, and library and archive records that share a name or topic. Pass unit_code to keep every signal inside one museum.

id.description: record_id of the anchor object (e.g. "nasm_A19670093000") from smithsonian_search_objects or smithsonian_get_object.

limit.description: Maximum number of related objects to return (default 10). A value above 1000 is served at 1000 with a notice.

start.description: Pagination offset — 0-indexed. Page contiguously by advancing start by the number of objects returned (a truncated page names the next start in its notice); each signal is reachable to a depth of 5000 objects, beyond which truncated stays true but deeper pages aren't retrievable.

unit_code.description: Scope every signal to one museum: the indexed unit code a result row's unit_code reports (e.g. "NASM"; the 3D scans are "OCIO_DPO3D"), never a holding_museum_name. Matched exactly and case-sensitively and not checked against the vocabulary — smithsonian_list_terms { field: "unit_code" } lists the codes. The anchor's own code keeps related objects in its museum; another code finds related objects held elsewhere. Omit it, or pass an empty string, to search every museum.
